first_impression.reaction: Googled 'greece wedding venues' because we're comparing three planners and Greece is on the list. The intro gives me hard numbers straight away, 40 people in Oia versus 1,000 on the Riviera, not 'breathtaking sunsets'. Went to the FAQ first as usual, then the comparison table, which is basically my spreadsheet done for me. Then I skimmed the venues I'd actually consider and read the legal section properly.

journey.quote: A caldera terrace in Oia suits 40 people. A Riviera resort half an hour from central Athens hosts up to 1,000.
journey.reaction: Two numbers in the first paragraph. That's how you get me to keep reading.

journey.section: Greece wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: They are not ranked. Each entry uses the same fields in the same order
journey.reaction: Good. No 'best of' nonsense, and same fields every time means I can actually compare. That's what I'd build myself.

journey.section: How to compare Greece wedding venues like for like
journey.quote: At Grace Hotel, the wedding venue fee covers exclusive use of the chosen event spaces, not the whole hotel, with a resort buyout available on request.
journey.reaction: This is exactly the catch I'd be worried about: 'exclusive use' meaning a terrace, not the hotel. Calling it out is the honest move.

journey.quote: "Not published" means the venue does not state it on its official pages.
journey.reaction: Plenty of blanks in that table, and they tell me it's a blank rather than filling it with a guess. I trust the filled-in numbers more because of it.

journey.quote: To check availability, ceremony options and house rules for your shortlist, speak with a Wedded Advisor, who quotes in AUD and works in your time zone.
journey.reaction: First pitch comes after a full table of numbers, so I'll let it slide. 'Quotes in AUD' is useful. Still makes me ask: quotes whose prices, and is there a margin on top?

journey.quote: The largest figures are outdoor ones, so plan your wet-weather fallback around the indoor number for the space you choose.
journey.reaction: That's the kind of trade-off a salesperson skips. 430 outdoors means nothing if it rains.

journey.quote: A larger Australian guest list will need a second hotel or a written room block agreement.
journey.reaction: Honest about a limitation of a venue they're listing. Good.

journey.quote: The resort closes on 14 November 2026 and reopens on 24 March 2027.
journey.reaction: Actual dates. I can check that in thirty seconds, which is the point.

journey.quote: Since 30 March 2026 the EU Entry/Exit System has been fully deployed for non-EU travellers, passport control may involve long waits, and the airport advises arriving at least 2.5 hours before departure.
journey.reaction: Dated and practical. My parents would be in that queue.

journey.section: Getting legally married in Greece as Australians, in brief
journey.quote: What fees apply, and to whom are they paid?
journey.reaction: Funny that they tell me to ask the town hall this and don't fully answer it about themselves. Still, a checklist of questions is more useful than a vague 'we handle the paperwork'.

journey.quote: On Santorini, most caldera terraces seat 20 to 60, so 100 guests needs a garden or pool space such as Canaves Epitome's.
journey.reaction: Straight answer with a named venue. That's what an FAQ is for.

journey.section: Shortlist your Greek venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal, fee in writing up front. Doesn't tell me how the fee is worked out or whether the venues pay you too.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues, and would that change which ones the Wedded Advisor recommends?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated and what does it cover?
Is the first conversation with a Wedded Advisor free?
Is there a real Greece wedding with the actual budget I can look at?
would_share_with: My fiancee, the comparison table and the 100-guest FAQ, since that's our number
My dad, the legal section and the airport queue point

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your date, your guest count and the venues you have in mind, and speak with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: The page earned it: numbers, dates, honest blanks, no hype, and the pitch comes after the evidence. This is the most useful of the three planner sites I've looked at for Greece. What stops a definite yes is the same question every time: do you take a cut from the venue? I'd want that answered before I hand over my guest list.

top_3_changes: Say, even in one line near the closing CTA, whether the Wedded Advisor takes commissions or mark-ups from venues (business detail deferred, so nice-to-have).
Say whether the first conversation is free and what it covers (business detail deferred, so nice-to-have).
Nothing else would stop me enquiring; no must-fix changes from me.

checks.check: Every journey point has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and table first, looked for numbers, dates, catches, fee model, commissions
No invented brand facts; missing fee, commission and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Title (person-set), deferred business details and unprinted prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or documentation lines, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: Is a fees or how-we-charge page available to link from the closing CTA? Business details are deferred, so treat as nice-to-have.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'greece wedding venues' while comparing three planners; Greece is a live option, hence high relevance.
No prices on the page is deliberate and not penalised.
